articles.title: Naomi Osaka makes grand entrance and big fashion statement at Australian Open
articles.summary: A statement of confidence as much as style, Naomi Osaka walked onto one of the biggest stages in tennis wearing a wide-brim hat, a veil and holding a white parasol in a bold opening act at the Australian Open.
articles.body: MELBOURNE, Australia — A statement of confidence as much as style, Naomi Osaka walked onto one of the biggest stages in tennis wearing a wide-brim hat, a veil and holding a white parasol in a bold opening act at the Australian Open. Aware that such an iconic walk-on could backfire if she lost her first-round match, Osaka did everything she needed Tuesday to bring down the curtain on Day 3 at Rod Laver Arena with a 6-3, 3-6, 6-4 victory over Antonia Ruzic. The hat and umbrella were adorned with symbolic butterflies, a nod to one of the memorable moments of Osaka's last title run at Melbourne Park in 2021 rather than a reflection of the usual first-round jitters at a major tournament. "When I was playing today, I just told myself, like, 'Keep your head on the path. If she beats you, then that's unfortunate. But, hey, at least you're trending,'" on social media, she said. Osaka has won four Grand Slam singles titles, including two at the U.S. Open and two in Australia in 2019 and 2021. She next plays Sorana Cirstea, who beat Eva Lys 3-6, 6-4, 6-3. After reaching the U.S. Open semifinals last year — her best result at a Grand Slam event in four years — Osaka is growing in confidence. Born in Japan but growing up in America, Osaka was inspired by Venus and Serena Williams and Maria Sharapova, the tennis stars she described as the "G.O.A.T's of style." "I think it all comes down to personality, too," she said. The dress she wore in her first-round match, in shades of blue and green, was also a tribute to her daughter, Shai, and her fascination with jellyfish. "So, the inspiration was obviously the jellyfish, then butterflies, which kind of ties back to the butterfly moment I had here a long time ago, in 2021," Osaka said, recalling the images of one landing on her during a third-round match. It took months of planning. And it all tied in with the remodelled player tunnel at Rod Laver Arena that reflects Australian themes such as beaches and the coast. "Honestly it came together quite beautifully because I didn't know what to expect when I arrived here," Osaka said. "Then it just felt like everywhere I looked the theme was water. Obviously the walkout was like you see oceans and waves. I thought that it was really beautiful. Really amazing coincidence."

articles.title: Nick Kyrgios: Controversial tennis player's career could be over after positive cocaine test
articles.summary: Nick Kyrgios once said he did not want to play tennis into his 30s. A positive cocaine test could have brought an end to his career aged 31.
articles.body:
Nick Kyrgios once said there was "zero chance" he would be playing tennis into his 30s.

But it was at the age of 31, while attempting another comeback from serious knee and wrist injuries, that he tested positive for a metabolite of cocaine at June's Mallorca Open.

In a post on social media, Kyrgios said it was a "huge mistake" for which he takes full responsibility.

But he added that recent injuries - he has only played eight tournaments and won two matches since the start of 2023 - have taken a huge toll on him.

"Coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined," he added.

Kyrgios will not be able to play until his case is resolved because of a mandatory provisional suspension.

But although he faces a potential ban of up to four years, his suspension would be limited to a maximum of three months if he can prove the drug was taken out of competition.

The Australian has achieved more than most on the sporting stage. As a 19-year-old in 2014 he stunned then world number one Rafael Nadal on his Centre Court debut, and finished runner-up at Wimbledon eight years later.

At his best, Kyrgios is a flamboyant and athletic shot-maker with flair, touch and an explosive game.

But he can also be destructive and verbally abusive, and has regularly struggled to sustain the levels of professionalism and abstinence needed for a prolonged stay at the very top.

In 2015, Kyrgios was given a suspended 28-day ban for making lewd remarks about Stan Wawrinka's girlfriend during a match in Montreal.

A year later, he was banned for eight weeks for his behaviour - including a "lack of best effort" - at the Shanghai Masters. This was reduced to three weeks after he agreed to consult a sports psychologist.

2019 was the nadir. Kyrgios was defaulted from a match at the Italian Open for hurling a chair on to the court, and was later fined $113,000 for verbally abusing umpire Fergus Murphy in Cincinnati.

The ATP later issued a suspended 16-week ban for a "pattern of behaviour related to his verbal abuse of officials and/or spectators" over the previous 12 months.

Kyrgios described 2019 as the "lowest point of my career" when interviewed for Netflix's Break Point documentary series.

"I was drinking, abusing drugs. I lost my relationship with my family, pushed all my close friends away," he said.

"Being bullied at a young age for being short and fat and brown scarred me for sure."

Kyrgios said he wore a compression sleeve to cover up self-harming scars on his arm and spent time in a psychiatric hospital in London to try and "figure out my problems".

He separately spoke about being forced out of a pub in Wimbledon Village by his agent in the early hours of a match day, and told Louis Theroux in 2024 that he would sometimes have "20 to 30 drinks" before playing the next day.

He has confessed to playing too much basketball - including for an hour before he beat David Ferrer in the 2017 Cincinnati Masters semi-finals - and has often said he has been unable to "dedicate" his life to tennis.

"I just enjoy doing whatever I'm doing," he said.

"I don't eat well. I don't train just for tennis, I train just for a general happy living - I know it sounds ridiculous, but I play a bit of tennis on the side."

In 2023, Kyrgios admitted assaulting ex-girlfriend Chiara Passari by pushing her on the pavement during a row in Canberra. The magistrate called the incident "a single act of stupidity or frustration" when sparing him a criminal record.

Then two years ago he publicly distanced himself from controversial influencer Andrew Tate, who is currently fighting extradition to the UK on charges including rape and offences related to sex trafficking.

Kyrgios told the BBC he had "deleted posts, unfollowed him and gone to all lengths to distance" himself from Tate.

The current world number 919 will now step away from public life for the next 28 days to "do the work and come back better".

The legal process could take many months - and Kyrgios is no fan of tennis' anti-doping system.

Describing the system as "awful," he made clear repeatedly his opinion that both Jannik Sinner and Iga Swiatek received overly lenient bans after their recent high-profile doping cases.

"Sad day for tennis. Fairness in tennis does not exist," Kyrgios wrote after Sinner accepted a three-month ban for testing positive for clostebol.

But if he does decide he wants to continue his career into his 30s, much will rest on the process of which Kyrgios has been so critical.

articles.title: Roger Federer Opens Up About Following Serena Williams in Tennis Comeback Ahead of US Open Return
articles.summary: Roger Federer is returning to the U.S. Open on Tuesday, albeit in a single-set exhibition against Andy Roddick and a set of doubles with John McEnroe against Roddick and Andre Agassi.
articles.body:
Roger Federer is returning to the U.S. Open on Tuesday, albeit in a single-set exhibition against Andy Roddick and a set of doubles with John McEnroe against Roddick and Andre Agassi.

But don't think he's looking to make a Serena Williams-esque comeback to competitive tennis.

"No, no, no, no. No, not at all," he told reporters when asked about the possibility. "Thanks for asking. I wasn't sure if the question was going to get asked, but I'm happy you did so I can clarify in case anybody thought."

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Williams, 44, made her comeback to professional tennis this summer, which included a singles appearance at Wimbledon. She lost her first-round matchup against Maya Joint , but it was nonetheless impressive to see her make a return after nearly four years off.

Federer, meanwhile, hasn't played competitive singles since the 2021 quarterfinals at Wimbledon. On Monday, he sounded more like a man nervous about a return to the court than one itching to get back to competition.

"I haven't played a singles set in, I don't know, (Hubert) Hurkacz at Wimbledon maybe, so it's been five years," he told reporters. "I don't know how it's going to go tomorrow. So there is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful moments."

He said he was looking forward to having something of a farewell moment with the U.S. Open fans, given he last played at the tournament in 2019, well before his retirement.

"They gave me an ovation because they saw me on the big screen, but I just feel, like, tomorrow and I guess today, as well, and Monday next week, it really gives me a true opportunity to say thank you and goodbye, which I think is important for some," he noted. "It's a nice thing to do, for sure."

articles.title: Serena Williams, Carlos Alcaraz drop quarterfinal match after opening-round win in US Open mixed doubles
articles.summary: Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up on Tuesday in a US Open return that was significant for both.
articles.body:
Serena Williams and Carlos Alcaraz teamed up Tuesday in mixed doubles for a US Open return that was significant for both.

They delivered with a comeback, 5-3, 4-1 win over mixed doubles specialists Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool in first-round play, much to the delight of a packed Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd that showed up to cheer on the tennis superstars.

They then fell in the quarterfinals to the fourth-seeded team of Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli, 5-4 (7-4), 4-1.

Serena, Alcaraz delight US Open crowd with first-round win

In the first round, Routliffe and Glasspool broke Alcaraz's first serve and took 2-0 and 3-1 leads in the first set. Sets on Tuesday were played to four games.

Then, trailing 3-2 with the first set on the line, Williams and Alcaraz scored their first break of the match to tie the set at 3-3. They survived two set points to stay alive. Williams then delivered with a pair of aces on her serve to take a 4-3 lead.

With a chance to set up game point on their next serve, Williams delivered a fiery forehand winner off a Routliffe serve.

Williams and Alcaraz followed through with their second break to secure the set, 5-3. They were in control from there. Routliffe and Glasspool won just one of the final eight games as Williams and Alcaraz put on a show for the supportive New York crowd.

"It's always such an amazing place to be here. I never expected to be back on this court," Williams said in her post-match interview. "It was just a really cool moment. I never thought this would happen."

Just minutes after their first-round win, Williams and Alcaraz took the Arthur Ashe Stadium court again in the quarterfinals. There, Bencic and Cobolli proved to be a significantly tougher test.

The two teams played to a tiebreak in the first set that Bencic and Cobolli won, 7-4. Williams hit a would-be winner long that allowed Bencic and Cobolli to extend their tiebreak lead to 6-4. Cobolli then sealed the first-set win with an ace.

Much like Williams and Alcaraz in their first match, Bencic and Cobolli were in control in the second set of the quarterfinals.

A Cobolli return forced a mishit by Alcaraz on game point in the fourth game, allowing Bencic and Cobolli to break and serve for the match, leading 3-1. Cobolli then delivered on his serve to secure the win and their place in the semifinals.

The win marked the fourth won set in four sets played for Bencic and Cobolli after they swept Taylor Townsend and Alexander Zverev earlier Tuesday. They'll take on Elina Svitolina and Gaël Monfils in the semifinals on Wednesday.

A comeback for both Williams and Alcaraz

For Williams, the match was her first at Arthur Ashe Stadium since her final pre-retirement singles match in 2022. She was back at the US Open on Tuesday competing with one of the biggest stars in the game in Alcaraz as part of a limited comeback to tennis. She will not play in the women's singles bracket.

Williams began her comeback in the spring that included a first-round singles loss at Wimbledon to Maya Joint. She's since played doubles with her sister, Venus, at the Cincinnati Open, where they lost in three sets in the first round to Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns.

For Alcaraz, the match marked his return to competitive tennis for the first time since he suffered a wrist injury in April that sidelined him for Wimbledon and the French Open. Alcaraz was initially listed in the field for the Cincinnati Open earlier in August, but he withdrew amid the lingering injury.

His nerves were apparent on the court as he started the first-round match with a double fault, but he settled into his game from there.

"I was out for four months and a half, almost five months," Alcaraz said after the first-round win. "I almost forget how it feels stepping on the court once again."

Now Alcaraz is back for the final Grand Slam of the year. Despite his rust, the two-time and reigning US Open champion is the favorite to win the men's singles title in a field that doesn't feature injured World No. 1 Jannik Sinner .

articles.title: Serena Williams Reacts to US Open Return in Video After Mixed Doubles with Carlos Alcaraz
articles.summary: Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2022 to compete alongside Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles at the U.S. Open.
articles.body:
Serena Williams returned to Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2022 to compete alongside Carlos Alcaraz in mixed doubles at the U.S. Open.

She and Alcaraz started things off with a win over Erin Routliffe and Lloyd Glasspool, and the tennis legend was thrilled to be back on the court.

"I never expected to be back on this court, so it was just a really cool moment," Williams said. "I never thought this would happen."

Williams has been out of action for much of the last four years but got a bit of a warm-up this summer as she participated in various tournaments. Despite so much time off, she looked more than comfortable alongside Alcaraz.

Alcaraz has also been away for a significant amount of time, missing the last four months with a wrist injury. Playing alongside an all-time great was nerve-wracking, but ultimately helped him ease back into it.

"I was really nervous playing alongside Serena," Alcaraz said. "... She made it really easy for me just to try to enjoy it, go for it every time."

Following the win in the opening round, Williams and Alcaraz lost to Belinda Bencic and Flavio Cobolli in the quarterfinals.

articles.title: Roger Federer Plays at US Open with John McEnroe, Andy Roddick, Agassi, Top Moments & Highlights
articles.summary: For one night, a legend was back on the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2019.
articles.body:
For one night, a legend was back on the court at Arthur Ashe Stadium for the first time since 2019.

Roger Federer participated in a special exhibition event on Tuesday ahead of the start of the main draw at this year's U.S. Open. The 20-time Grand Slam champion was joined by Andy Roddick, John McEnroe and Andre Agassi for the celebratory matches.

Federer faced Roddick in a set of singles competition before teaming with McEnroe to go against Roddick and Agassi.

Agassi, Serena and more iconic US Open outfits

Perhaps the first hint at the magnitude of the night was the reaction Federer received before a coin toss that featured another notable name:

Once the tennis started, it was clear Federer hadn't lost his skills.

He cruised to a 6-3 victory over Roddick behind a powerful serve and some of his famous backhands:

It was an impressive showing considering how long he has been away from the game.

"I haven't played a singles set in, I don't know, (Hubert) Hurkacz at Wimbledon maybe, so it's been five years," Federer said Monday, per Brian Mahoney of the Associated Press. "I don't know how it's going to go tomorrow. So there is a lot of uncertainty but a lot of happiness that I can return to Arthur Ashe, a place where I have had so many beautiful moments."

The fans were happy to remember those beautiful moments Tuesday as they watched him play on the same court he enjoyed so much success on during the peak of his career.

Federer won five consecutive U.S. Open men's singles titles from 2004 through 2008. He also reached the final again in 2009 and 2015 and was a fan favorite for much of his run.

Those moments all came during his singles career, but he also mixed it up in the doubles match that was filled with notable names in the second half of Tuesday's performance.

He and McEnroe defeated Roddick and Agassi, 7-5, in a match that let all four of them show off their skills at various times.

articles.title: Who is Andy Roddick's wife? Meet Brooklyn Decker, the actress and model married to the tennis legend
articles.summary: International Sports News: Andy Roddick won a US Open title in 2003 and spent years ranked No. 1 in the world, but his personal life has drawn nearly as much attention as his te.
articles.body: Andy Roddick won a US Open title in 2003 and spent years ranked No. 1 in the world, but his personal life has drawn nearly as much attention as his tennis career. His wife, Brooklyn Decker, is a familiar name in both fashion and Hollywood. The couple met in 2007, got engaged in 2008, and wed on April 17, 2009. They have been together for nearly two decades now, raising two kids and building a life far removed from the tennis circuit. Here is everything worth knowing about who Brooklyn Decker is and how their relationship took shape.How did Andy Roddick and Brooklyn Decker meet?The origin story is less romantic dinner, more cold DM. Andy Roddick first saw Decker hosting a Sports Illustrated football show online. He reached out to her, and she eventually agreed to connect. What followed moved fast. They dated for about a year before he proposed, and the two got engaged in March 2008.Roddick himself admitted the whole thing caught him off guard. "I went from, 'I don't think I'm gonna get in a serious relationship forever,' and then we were engaged in, like, six months. And then we really got to know each other," he told GQ in 2023.They married at Roddick's private home in Austin, Texas. Decker wore a Vera Wang gown for the evening ceremony, and Elton John performed for the couple and their guests at the celebration that followed. She was 21 at the time; Roddick was 26.Balancing the marriage was not always straightforward. Roddick was still an active player, traveling for tournaments, while Decker had her own demanding schedule. He later said the engagement itself was what held them together through those stretches apart. "If we hadn't actually made that commitment, I don't know that we would get through that."They have two children together. Son Hank was born in October 2015, and daughter Stevie arrived in 2017. Decker has described their current family dynamic with characteristic humor. "Marriage does become hilariously transactional," she told Us Weekly. "You're like, 'I've got the kids, you go buy the tampons, go get the diapers.' It's very like making a game plan for a football game."Who is Brooklyn Decker beyond her marriage to Andy Roddick?Most people first encountered Brooklyn Decker through a magazine cover. She appeared in the Sports Illustrated Swimsuit Issue starting in 2006 before landing the cover of the 2010 edition, one of the most visible spots in the modeling world at the time. That visibility opened doors in Hollywood.Her film debut came in 2011 with Just Go with It alongside Adam Sandler and Jennifer Aniston. She followed that with roles in Battleship and What to Expect When You're Expecting, but her most sustained acting work came on the small screen. In 2015, she took on the role of Mallory Hanson in the Netflix series Grace and Frankie, playing the daughter of Jane Fonda's character. The role ran for 28 episodes across all seven seasons, ending in 2022.Decker has spoken openly about how the transition from modeling to acting was a deliberate choice, not a fallback. "The Sports Illustrated cover was the last thing I shot. I told my agent, 'I don't want to be a model anymore. I really want to do movies.'"Beyond the screen, she co-created a digital wardrobe app called Finery, which was later acquired by Stitch Fix. She also serves as a global ambassador for the Special Olympics.Roddick's retirement from tennis in 2012 changed the texture of their family life considerably. As Decker put it during a 2017 Tennis Channel interview: "He's an unbelievable dad, incredibly hands-on. I feel so thankful that it happened after he retired, because he's here every day with them."In April 2026, the couple marked their 17th wedding anniversary. Decker posted a photo on Instagram of the two in colonial costumes, joking that the years have felt much longer than they actually have. Fitting for a couple that has, in many ways, built something more interesting than either of their careers alone.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Roger Federer rolls back years to beat Andy Roddick in exhibition at US Open
articles.summary: New York fans enjoyed a vintage Federer singles win before the 20-time Grand Slam champion teamed up with John McEnroe to beat Andy Roddick and Andre Agassi; watch the 2026 US Open live on Sky Sports Tennis and Sky Sports+, NOW and the Sky Sports app
articles.body:
Roger Federer made a triumphant return to the US Open court with a pair of exhibition victories in front of an adoring Arthur Ashe Stadium crowd in New York on Tuesday.

The event, billed as "An Icon Returns to New York", packed the stands with fans eager to watch the 45-year-old Swiss star face Andy Roddick, who is soon to turn 44, in a prime-time exhibition.

Federer defeated Roddick in an opening singles match before teaming up with John McEnroe to win a doubles exhibition against Roddick and Andre Agassi.

  • Download Sky Sports app for analysis, news and video 📺
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract 📱

Federer, a 20-time Grand Slam champion, returned to the court at the US Open for the first time since 2019.

The Swiss legend won five consecutive US Open men's singles titles between 2004 and 2008, tying Pete Sampras and Jimmy Connors for the most in the Open era.

"It's great to be back in New York," Federer said. "It's incredible.

"I have incredible memories of this court, the fans here and the city. In 2004 and 2005, that's when it all started here, my love for New York, with the victories here."

He added: "I fell in love with this city and this court from day one.

"I believe my first time on Centre Court was against Andre [Agassi] in 2001. He smashed me 6-1, 6-2, 6-4. I had no shot. I was like, 'Okay, not so easy, not so fast, Roger.'"

articles.title: “Whatever I Feel Doesn’t Matter”- Andy Roddick Reacts as American Tennis Eyes US Open History
articles.summary: It has been 23 years since Andy Roddick won his US Open title, and the country is still in search of its next men’s Grand Slam champion. Roddick was present...
articles.body:
It has been 23 years since Andy Roddick won his US Open title, and the country is still in search of its next men's Grand Slam champion. Roddick was present at Arthur Ashe on Tuesday and, along with another great, Andre Agassi, expressed hope that the American men's contingent would end the long wait.

"Well whatever I feel doesn't matter as much as the support they get inside of the building," said Roddick after his doubles match against Roger Federer and John McEnroe. "You all will play a big part in doing it, so I hope it happens and that you all will help them along the way."

With the likes of Jannik Sinner out with an injury, and with Carlos Alcaraz coming back after a long injury layoff, the chances for an American champion at this year's US Open are high. Of the 32 seeds in the men's draw, six are American, with the likes of Ben Shelton and Taylor Fritz being the best bets for the title for the American men.

Not only Roddick, but even Agassi was optimistic about the chances of his compatriots at the Flushing Meadows over the next two weeks.

There's real momentum building around the American men at the US Open right now. Subscribe for more interesting stories.

"I think we have a great group of Americans right now and this might just be the two weeks one of them show that it can be get done," said Agassi during the on-court interview.

The two American legends teamed up against the pair of Federer and McEnroe in an exhibition event which celebrated the Swiss player's comeback on Arthur Ashe after seven years. It was a loss for the all-American team, and Roddick went on to lose his singles match against Federer as well, but will hope for better American fortunes for the top-ranked American players in the men's draw.

Up until a couple of years ago, Roddick was not only the last American player to win a Slam, but also the last American player to reach a Slam final at the 2009 Wimbledon. However, the latter record was taken from Roddick's name, with Taylor Fritz reaching the US Open final in 2024.

The hard-court warm-up events before the US Open have seen decent results for some American players, increasing their chances heading into Flushing Meadows next week. Taylor Fritz won the title in Washington, with Ben Shelton in supreme form at the Canadian Open, successfully defending his title. Even Frances Tiafoe had a great warm-up for New York, reaching the final of the Cincinnati Open.

However, this is not the first time that Roddick has had bullish expectations from his compatriots at a Grand Slam. Before Wimbledon, the former American pro was confident that one of the American players would reach the semifinals, with Alcaraz not at SW19. Roddick's confidence was understandable: Tiafoe and Shelton had both won grass-court titles before Wimbledon, beating Fritz in the respective finals.

But Shelton struggled to meet expectations, losing in the first round, whereas Tiafoe gave away several opportunities to take the lead and lost in the third round. Fritz was the only one who went deep but lost to Alexander Zverev in the quarterfinals, with the American struggling with knee injuries.

With the American crowd behind them, one can expect that the top American players will have a better time at Flushing Meadows. All three of the American favorites have had their best Slam moments at the US Open, which is where Roddick and Agassi hope the American men can finally end the Grand Slam drought.
